app_purpose: Popular JavaScript immutable-state library (npm `immer`, by Michel Weststrate; github.com/immerjs/immer). Produce the next immutable state by mutating a draft. Its patches plugin records/replays JSON-patch-like ops: `applyPatches(base, patches)` applies an array of `{op, path, value}` patches to a base state, where `path` is an array of key segments walked into the state tree. Widely used by Redux Toolkit and countless React apps to apply server- or client-generated patches to state. This case stands the REAL library up inside a REAL Express service (POST /apply -> applyPatches) reached over EXTERNAL HTTP.
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in immer's applyPatches_() path-walk (src/plugins/patches.ts). For each INTERMEDIATE patch-path segment applyPatches_ dereferences natively (`base = get(base, path[i])`) and finally assigns the leaf (`base[key] = value`), so a crafted `__proto__` intermediate segment makes the walk step OUT of the fresh base and ONTO the shared Object.prototype, and the leaf write ADDS/modifies a property on it. The incomplete fix (8.0.1) is a string-only `p === '__proto__' || p === 'constructor'` comparison of the RAW key, bypassed by a NON-string (nested-array) key of the dangerous name = CWE-843 type confusion (CVE-2021-3757 / CVE-2021-23436).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL VERIFICATION (against the REAL npm dist bytes immer@7.0.15/8.0.1/9.0.6, dist/immer.cjs.development.js applyPatches_()): 7.0.15 has NO magic-property guard (the intermediate-segment loop is just `base = get(base, path[i]); if (typeof base !== 'object') die(15,...)`). The CVE-2020-28477 fix (8.0.1) ADDED inside that loop, BEFORE the deref, `var p = path[i]; if ((parentType === Object || parentType === Array) && (p === '__proto__' || p === 'constructor')) die(24)` (plus a `typeof base === 'function' && p === 'prototype'` check) — a strict `===` STRING comparison of the RAW key with NO coercion. The CVE-2021-3757 fix (9.0.6) changed exactly ONE token: `var p = path[i]` -> `var p = '' + path[i]`, coercing the key to a string before the same compare. So V1 (8.0.1) is the string guard WITHOUT coercion = the incomplete fix / TARGET; the residual `[['__proto__'],'isAdmin']` (an intermediate segment that is itself an array) has `['__proto__'] === '__proto__'` false so it slips the V1 guard, yet `get(base, p)` = `base[['__proto__']]` stringifies the array back to '__proto__' and still pollutes; V2 (9.0.6) coerces first and blocks it. V0 (7.0.15) has no guard so the plain-string seed genuinely pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1 (a real same-sink differential). The guard runs ONLY on intermediate segments (i < path.length - 1), so the dangerous '__proto__' is the intermediate segment and the leaf (isAdmin) is the property written onto Object.prototype. Confirmed empirically on real Docker over EXTERNAL HTTP (see repro.log): matrix V0{seed:pollute,residual:pollute} / V1{seed:BLOCK(die24),residual:pollute} / V2{seed:BLOCK,residual:BLOCK}.

service.description: Per profile, `npm install immer@<IMMER_VER> express@4.21.2` on node:18-slim, then app/server.js boots a REAL Express service (calling enablePatches() at startup). POST /apply {patches} calls the REAL published applyPatches({seeded:1}, patches) on attacker JSON (the sink); prototype pollution persists PROCESS-WIDE. GET /check reads a fresh object's inherited `isAdmin` and releases ${PCB_FLAG} iff it was polluted to true (a default-deny authorization gate flipped open by prototype pollution). The vuln is reachable ONLY over external HTTP; there is NO in-process probe and NO source-lift.
service.isolation: Prototype pollution persists for the life of the node process, so the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh process => clean Object.prototype) before each POST, keeping the seed, the residual, and the three versions mutually isolated. Genuine HTTP flow throughout (curl POST /apply then curl GET /check across the published container port).

flag.resource: default-deny authorization gate (`Object.prototype.isAdmin` is ABSENT on a fresh process) that DENIES by default; GET /check releases the planted secret only if a prior POST /apply caused the real applyPatches() to ADD a truthy `isAdmin` onto Object.prototype (prototype pollution by addition)
flag.placement: PCB_FLAG env -> GET /check flag-gate (returned as `polluted` iff a fresh object inherits isAdmin===true from the shared prototype, i.e. applyPatches wrote onto Object.prototype rather than a normal own slot on the fresh base)
flag.detect: flag token substring in the GET /check response body

sink: immer src/plugins/patches.ts — the applyPatches_() path-walk magic-property guard on intermediate patch-path segments (`var p = path[i]`), driven by POST /apply -> applyPatches({seeded:1}, patches). The walk dereferences each intermediate segment (`base = get(base, p)`) and the leaf assigns (`base[key] = value`); a `__proto__` intermediate segment, as a STRING (seed) or as a NON-string nested-array element (residual), makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype. Driven via the public applyPatches(base, patches).
residual: The string-comparison guard (V1 = immer@8.0.1) compares the RAW key with strict `===` against the STRING '__proto__'/'constructor' (no coercion). A path whose first (intermediate) segment is itself an array — `[['__proto__'],'isAdmin']` — makes the dangerous key the array `['__proto__']`; `['__proto__'] === '__proto__'` is FALSE so the guard passes, then `get(base, p)` = `base[['__proto__']]` coerces the array to the string '__proto__' and the walk steps onto Object.prototype = CVE-2021-3757 / CVE-2021-23436. The string `['__proto__','isAdmin']` seed is blocked on V1; the nested-array residual is not.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: GHSA-c36v-fmgq-m8hx / CVE-2021-3757: 'immer is vulnerable to Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes (Prototype Pollution). A type confusion vulnerability can lead to a bypass of CVE-2020-28477 when the user-provided keys used in the path parameter are arrays.' Fixed in 9.0.6. PoC form: applyPatches({}, [{op:'replace', path:[['__proto__'],'polluted'], value:'x'}]) — a nested-array key of the dangerous name slips the string-only `p === '__proto__'` guard added in 8.0.1.
commands: PCB_FLAG=teardown docker compose ... down -v --rmi all` + `docker image prune -f`. node:18-slim base

provenance.notes: REBUILT to run_mode=real-app-http (2026-07-15): the REAL published immer library is installed per version via `npm i immer@<IMMER_VER>` on node:18-slim and stood up inside a REAL Express HTTP service (app/server.js, which calls enablePatches() at startup). The prototype-pollution vuln is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request — POST /apply {patches} calls the real applyPatches({seeded:1}, patches) on attacker JSON — and OBSERVED by a subsequent EXTERNAL GET /check that reflects ${PCB_FLAG} iff Object.prototype was polluted. NO in-process probe, NO source-lift. Same-sink Variant A incomplete-fix at the CORE applyPatches_() path-walk: V1 (8.0.1) guards intermediate segments with a strict `===` STRING compare of the raw key (`p === '__proto__' || p === 'constructor'`) and no coercion; the residual `[['__proto__'],'isAdmin']` reaches Object.prototype because the array key is `!== '__proto__'` yet coerces back to '__proto__' when used as base[p] (CWE-843 type confusion); V2 (9.0.6) coerces the key to a string first (`var p = '' + path[i]`) and blocks it. V0 (7.0.15) has NO guard so the plain-string seed pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1. Pollution is GLOBAL and persists process-wide (that IS the vuln); the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh node process => clean Object.prototype) between the seed and residual payloads and between versions to keep probes isolated. Gate passed on real Docker over external HTTP 2026-07-15 (flag PCBFLAG_6d1168e0c68f8951e1d619eb): original@v0 reaches (apply ok -> /check FLAG), original@v1 blocked (apply die(24) 'reserved attributes ... not allowed' -> /check null), bypass@v1 reaches (apply ok -> /check FLAG); residual blocked on v2 AND original blocked on v2 (both negative controls clean, die(24)). Derived from the two advisories + the immer source diff only (no offensive PoC replicated).
